unit.title: Virtue and habit I
unit.needIt: This helps you build better habits by turning 'shoulds' into 'just do it' actions. You can use it to stop scrolling on your phone by rewarding yourself for reading a book instead.
unit.why: Aristotle taught that we become brave by doing brave acts. Today, we see how our brains turn these repeated actions into automatic laws of nature.
unit.outcome: Create a plan to turn a goal into a daily habit using rewards.

quiz.q: What is the difference between a descriptive law and a normative law?
choices: Descriptive is a rule; normative is a fact
Descriptive is how things are; normative is how they ought to be
Normative laws only apply to animals
quiz.why: Descriptive laws describe facts of the world, while normative laws express how things should be.
quiz.quote: Because gravity isn't a law that tells you how you ought to behave. It's a law that tells you how things do behave.

choices: A rule of how to behave
quiz.why: Normative laws are about how things ought to be, like rules or norms.
quiz.quote: They are laws in the sense that you find over at the Yale law school.

quiz.why: Descriptive laws describe how things actually are, like gravity or biology.
quiz.quote: They tell you the way things actually are.

quiz.q: How does Aristotle say we learn a craft?
quiz.why: Aristotle argues that we become what we do by repeatedly performing the action.
quiz.quote: So when Aristotle says we learn a craft by producing the same product that we must produce when we've learned it

quiz.q: What is the main goal of parenting mentioned?
quiz.why: Parenting aims to make good choices automatic so children do them without thinking.
quiz.quote: one of the main goals of parenting is to instill in one's children instinctive responses that accord with reflective commitments.

quiz.q: Why is it hard to change habits just by talking to yourself?
choices: We are not just composed of reason
Talking is a waste of time
quiz.why: The lecture explains that humans have biological and emotional parts that do not always follow logic.
quiz.quote: Part of the reason that at least 65% of you fall into the category of people who are unable to talk yourself out of an unwanted behavior is that we aren't just composed of reason.

quiz.why: It focuses on how our own actions lead to specific consequences or rewards.
quiz.quote: Operant conditioning is concerned with the relation between behaviors that you yourself perform and the outcomes to which those behaviors typically give rise.

partials: Normative laws are about how we ought to act.

crystal.key: Habits turn conscious choices into automatic laws of behavior.

decoys.why: Aristotle says arguments alone are often not enough to change long-held habits.

decoys.text: Punishment is the best way to stop a habit.
decoys.why: The lecture suggests rewarding the opposite behavior is more effective than punishment.

crystal.aha: By repeating actions and using rewards, we turn our goals into our natural reality.
